items.q: The first session of dialysis should be kept shorter than:
items.exp: Dialysis disequilibrium syndrome: the first session of dialysis should be <1 hour, with subsequent sessions of 4 hours. (Book p781)

items.q: The duration of subsequent dialysis sessions recommended after the first short session is:
items.exp: First session <1 hour; subsequent sessions 4 hours, to avoid dialysis disequilibrium syndrome. (Book p781)

items.q: Complete the dialysis disequilibrium flowchart — 1) Urea in the blood compartment  2) Effect on blood osmolality  3) Consequence in cells … A) Cerebral edema → seizure, death  B) ↓ Osmolality  C) Rapidly moves to the dialysate compartment
items.exp: Flowchart: urea rapidly moves from blood to dialysate → blood osmolality falls → water moves into cells → cerebral oedema → seizure and death. (Book p781)

items.q: Dialysis disequilibrium syndrome occurs because urea is removed so quickly that the osmolality of the blood compartment falls.
opts: False — blood osmolality rises during dialysis
False — the syndrome is caused by water leaving the cells
True, but the fall in osmolality causes intracellular dehydration
items.exp: Urea moves rapidly into the dialysate, dropping blood osmolality; water then moves into cells, producing cerebral oedema with seizure and death if dialysis is continued beyond 2 hours. (Book p781)

items.q: A severely uraemic patient receives a 4-hour first dialysis session and develops headache, confusion and a seizure. The mechanism is:
opts: Water movement into cells after a rapid fall in blood osmolality — cerebral edema
Rapid movement of water out of cells causing cerebral dehydration
items.exp: Dialysis disequilibrium: rapid urea removal → ↓ blood osmolality → water moves into cells (including brain) → cerebral oedema, seizure and death. (Book p781)

items.q: Which statement correctly summarises the prevention of dialysis disequilibrium syndrome?
opts: Limit the first dialysis session to less than 1 hour, with 4-hour subsequent sessions
Give the first session for 6 hours to clear urea completely
Avoid dialysis in uraemic patients altogether
Use only peritoneal dialysis in all uraemic patients
items.exp: Prevention: the first dialysis session should be <1 hour; subsequent sessions are 4 hours, because continuing beyond 2 hours risks cerebral oedema. (Book p781)
